pods = [

    "recommendationservice-0", "recommendationservice-1", "recommendationservice-2", "recommendationservice2-0",
    "paymentservice-0", "paymentservice-1", "paymentservice-2", "paymentservice2-0"
]
services = [
    "frontend", "shippingservice", "checkoutservice", "currencyservice",
    "adservice", "emailservice", "cartservice", "productcatalogservice",
    "recommendationservice", "paymentservice"
]

# Filter metrics data for possible root cause components
# The metric_df may have different columns for different metric types:
# For service metrics: 'service' column exists
# For others: 'cmdb_id' column exists
# We will filter rows where either 'cmdb_id' or 'service' matches the root cause components

# Create a mask for rows with cmdb_id in nodes or pods
mask_cmdb = metric_df['cmdb_id'].isin(nodes + pods) if 'cmdb_id' in metric_df.columns else pd.Series([False]*len(metric_df))
# Create a mask for rows with service in services
mask_service = metric_df['service'].isin(services) if 'service' in metric_df.columns else pd.Series([False]*len(metric_df))

# Combine masks
mask = mask_cmdb | mask_service

filtered_metric_df = metric_df[mask]

# Extract unique KPI names from filtered data
# For service metrics, KPI columns are rr, sr, mrt, count (no kpi_name column)
# For other metrics, KPI names are in 'kpi_name' column

    # For service metrics, list the KPI columns if present

    existing_kpi_cols = [col for col in kpi_cols if col in filtered_metric_df.columns]
    unique_kpis = pd.DataFrame(existing_kpi_cols, columns=['kpi_name'])
